neighbours.label: Counterfactual perfect: ' have' or the next verb after would, should, could or might ('would have killed', 'should have succeeded'); the plain past of the same events stays quiet
fire: The flood would have ruined the town.
You wouldn't have won without the coach.
I would have liked to see the show.
We should have left earlier, had we known.
If I had seen it, I would have stopped.
The bomb would have destroyed the bridge.
She could have been a great singer.
They might have survived had help come.
quiet: The flood ruined the town last year.
You won a prize from the coach.
We left earlier than we planned.
I saw it, and I stopped.
